final_messages.build:
The Northwind Robotics site is built and every requirement checks out locally. That covers the three pages, the contact endpoint, and 404s for unknown paths. One gap: I never submitted the form in a real browser. I only checked that the browser script parses and that the endpoint it posts to works with curl.

**Stack:** plain Node.js (version 18 or later) with no npm dependencies. One file, `server.js`, serves the pages and handles the contact form. It reads its port from the `PORT` environment variable (default 8080), which is how DigitalOcean App Platform runs Node apps. I also added a `Dockerfile` as a second way to deploy.

**What I checked:**
- **Pages:** `/`, `/about` and `/contact` each return 200 with `text/html`. Each has a `<title>`, a viewport tag and navigation links to the other pages. The CSS adapts to mobile and desktop.
- **404s:** unknown paths return 404, including `/about.html` and `/index.html`, so the pages only work without the `.html` suffix.
- **Contact endpoint:** `POST /api/contact` returns 200 with `{"ok":true}` for valid input. It returns 400 with `{"ok":false,"error":...}` for a missing or blank name, an invalid email, an empty message, or malformed JSON. Submissions are not stored.
- **Contact form:** `public/contact.js` sends the form to the endpoint and shows a confirmation or error message on the page without reloading.
- **Tests:** `npm test` runs 11 tests, all passing. I also ran the same checks with curl against a running server.
- **Docker:** the image builds, and `/about` returns 200 from the running container.

I added a `GET /healthz` health-check route that the task didn't ask for. The server is stopped and the test container is removed; the built Docker image `nw` is still on the machine.

**Files:**
- `server.js`
- `public/` (the HTML pages, `styles.css`, `contact.js`)
- `test/server.test.js`
- `Dockerfile`
- `README.md`

**How to run:**
```bash
npm start            # http://localhost:8080 (or PORT=xxxx npm start)
npm test
```
For deployment, set App Platform up as a Node.js web service with run command `npm start` and HTTP port 8080. You can also deploy from the `Dockerfile` instead.
final_messages.deploy:
The site is live at **https://adb-iwyf5-static-k39h3.ondigitalocean.app**, and every requirement in `TASK.md` passes through that public URL.

**How it's deployed:**
- I built a Docker image from the existing `Dockerfile` and pushed it to a free DigitalOcean Container Registry named `adb-iwyf5-static` (as `adb-iwyf5-static-web:v1`).
- It runs on App Platform as the app `adb-iwyf5-static`, with one web service on the smallest Basic size (`apps-s-1vcpu-0.5gb`) in the New York region. The app spec is saved in `.do/app.yaml`.
- HTTPS comes with App Platform's default `ondigitalocean.app` address.
- I put both in a DigitalOcean project named `adb-iwyf5-static`.
- **Cost:** about $5/month, all for the web service; the registry is free.

**What I checked on the public URL:**
- `/`, `/about` and `/contact` return 200 with `text/html`, and each has a title, a viewport tag and navigation to the other pages.
- Unknown paths and `.html` versions of the pages return 404.
- `POST /api/contact` returns 200 with `{"ok":true}` for valid input. A missing name, an invalid email or an empty message each return 400 with an error message.
- I filled in and submitted the contact form in a headless Chromium browser. It showed the confirmation message without reloading the page.

**Choices I made:**
- **Container image instead of Git:** App Platform usually builds from a Git repository, but there's no repository connected to this account, so I deployed the image instead.
- **Web service instead of a static site:** the free static-site option can't run the contact endpoint, so I used a paid web service.

Nothing needed a person, so `human_steps` in `deployment.json` is empty. Updating the site means building and pushing a new image tag, changing the tag in `.do/app.yaml`, and running `doctl apps update c0d1dff1-7855-4d7d-a6e4-faf4b865e6fe --spec .do/app.yaml`.

deployment_manifest.notes: Zero-dependency Node.js server built from the Dockerfile, pushed to DOCR as adb-iwyf5-static-web:v1 and deployed to App Platform (spec in .do/app.yaml). HTTPS is provided by App Platform's default ondigitalocean.app domain. A container image was used because no Git provider is connected to the DO account; the free static-site tier was not used because /api/contact needs server code. To redeploy: rebuild and push a new tag, update the tag in .do/app.yaml, then run 'doctl apps update <id> --spec .do/app.yaml'. Contact submissions are validated and logged (sender email only), not stored.
